definitions.explanation: The buttocks or gluteal region of the body. A clinical/anatomical term used in medicine, fitness, and formal writing. In everyday speech Japanese speakers use the much more common お{尻|しり} (or plain {尻|しり}).

examples.japanese: {臀部|でんぶ}に{痛|いた}みがある。
examples.english: I have pain in the buttocks.

examples.japanese: {医師|いし}は{臀部|でんぶ}に{注射|ちゅうしゃ}を{打|う}った。
examples.english: The doctor gave an injection in the buttocks.

examples.japanese: この{筋|きん}トレは{臀部|でんぶ}と{太|ふと}ももの{筋肉|きんにく}を{同時|どうじ}に{鍛|きた}えられる。
examples.english: This strength exercise trains the gluteal and thigh muscles at the same time.

notes:
Composed of {臀|でん} ("buttocks") + {部|ぶ} ("part, region"). A Sino-Japanese medical/anatomical term found mainly in clinical contexts, anatomy textbooks, pharmaceutical instructions (e.g., "apply to the {臀部|でんぶ}"), and fitness writing. The kanji {臀|でん} is not commonly written by hand and is often left in kana (でんぶ) in informal anatomy references.

REGISTER:
- Formal and clinical; avoid in casual speech.
- In everyday conversation, use お{尻|しり} (polite/neutral) or {尻|しり} (blunt).
- In fitness and bodybuilding contexts, お{尻|しり}, ヒップ, and {臀部|でんぶ} coexist; {臀部|でんぶ} sounds the most technical.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {臀部|でんぶ}の{筋肉|きんにく}: the gluteal muscles
- {臀部|でんぶ}に{注射|ちゅうしゃ}する: to inject into the buttocks
- {臀部|でんぶ}{痛|つう}: pain in the buttocks
- {臀部|でんぶ}を{鍛|きた}える: to train/strengthen the glutes

SIMILAR WORDS:
- お{尻|しり}: buttocks — the everyday, all-purpose word; appropriate in almost any non-clinical context
- {尻|しり}: buttocks — blunt/rough register; also used figuratively (e.g., {尻|しり}が{重|おも}い)
- {ヒップ}: hips/buttocks — loanword, common in fashion and fitness
- {大殿筋|だいでんきん}: gluteus maximus — a specific muscle within the {臀部|でんぶ}

RELATED TERMS:
- {腰|こし}: lower back, hips
- {骨盤|こつばん}: pelvis
- {太|ふと}もも: thigh
